Tick Isolated on a Bot to give it a container of its own. Set `COMPUTER_RUNTIME=runsc` to run them under gVisor where the host supports it. - **A shell, not just a browser**: a Bot can run a command in its workspace, install what it needs, and process a file it saved. Through the same gate as everything else, so a rule can refuse a shell outright or refuse particular commands, and the command is on the record either way. The command inherits PATH, locale, terminal and proxy variables, not the rest of the deployment's environment. - **The gateway is the only way in**: it resolves the target from a server-held snapshot, evaluates the policy, writes the audit row, and only then calls the computer. There is no path that acts without the record existing first. - **CEL policy, fail closed**: rules can inspect `tool.name`, `intent`, `bot.id`, `actor.id`, `page.url`, `page.host`, `element.*`, `key`, `command`, `file.*`, `mcp.*` and `initiator.*` (what started the run, so a rule can refuse a scheduled routine what it would allow a person). Deny is evaluated before allow, a missing policy permits nothing, and a broken rule refuses rather than opens. - **Watch what it is doing**: the screen shows what a Bot is looking at, and the Activity list under it shows what it ran, read and saved in this conversation, with the output. A command line in the transcript opens to the same thing. A saved file shows its path and size, never its contents. - **Take the wheel**: a Bot that hits a login wall or a 2FA prompt asks for help. Control is handed over in the same panel and recorded as `computer.help_requested`, `computer.control_taken` and `computer.control_released`. While a person is driving, Bot actions are refused rather than queued. - **Secrets never enter the transcript**: the trail records that a secret was requested and how long it was, not what it said. - **Bring your own agent**: any AG-UI endpoint is a Bot, on a framework or hand-written. Endpoints are validated with the same target checks used for browser navigation, and an auth header is stored write-only. - **Components instead of prose**: compiled React components live in `app/src/components/gallery/`, sandboxed ones are authored in `/admin/playground` and published with no deployment. Every call asks the server whether the component exists, is published, and is not withheld from that Bot. Data functions are granted per component. - **Governed MCP**: Google Drive, Notion and the [public-web research providers](docs/web-research.md) Parallel, Exa and Firecrawl ship in the catalogue, and Composio brokers a few hundred more apps behind one account (Arcade can be the broker instead), each reached as the person asking. The catalogue carries only vendors this deployment stands behind, so adding one is a review of that vendor. Custom servers must pass URL checks; unknown tools and custom-server tools are treated as writes, and a catalogue tool the server advertises but does not name as a write classifies as a read. A Bot is told which connectors exist here and which it holds, so it says it has not been granted one rather than browsing to the vendor's website. - **Skills are instructions, not capabilities**: personal skills attach only to Bots their author owns, deployment skills are admin-owned, and both are invoked with `/` in the composer. A Bot granted the shipped `skill-creator` skill can write one with you in the conversation, and saves it only when you press the button on the card. - **Sign in with what your company already has**: Google, Microsoft or Okta from the environment, or a company's own SAML or OpenID Connect provider registered while the deployment runs and routed by email domain. Any one turns sign-in on; several may be configured at once. - **Decide who gets in**: `/admin/people` lists everybody who has signed in, promotes and demotes them, and removes access, which ends the session they are using and stops the next sign-in. Every change is on the audit trail. - **An audit trail you can read**: `/admin/audit` lists what was permitted, what was refused and what failed, and every refusal carries the rule that caused it. - **Credentials encrypted at rest**: stored through `/admin/credentials`, never returned by an API, and redacted from audit events. - **Loopback by default**: computers bind to `127.0.0.1` and require a per-container token, so nothing reaches a logged-in browser by knowing its port. The supervisor binds there too, because it holds the Docker socket and its token is a shared secret rather than a network boundary. - **Durable threads and memory**: conversations survive restarts through CopilotKit Intelligence, and each deployment stamps the threads it owns. - **Routines**: ask a Bot to do something on a schedule and it does, running as you, in the channel you asked in. A 15-minute floor and a cap of 20 enabled routines keep a sentence from scheduling more than a person meant, and ten failures in a row switch a routine off rather than burn model spend forever. The server fires them itself, so there is nothing else to run; see [docs/routines.md](docs/routines.md). ## Bring your own agent Any AG-UI endpoint can be a Bot. From `/bots`, create a Bot with: - name and instructions, which become its role description; - private or public visibility; - optional AG-UI endpoint, with the framework the agent is built on when it is one New Bot lists; - optional write-only authorization header. The server validates agent endpoints with the same target checks used for browser navigation, at registration and again on every redirect the endpoint answers with. If no custom endpoint is set, product-created coworkers use `MANAGED_AGENT_AG_UI_URL` when it is configured, and otherwise run in the OpenBot server on their role description. A private address is refused unless it is listed in `AGENT_ENDPOINT_ALLOWED_HOSTS`: ```sh AGENT_ENDPOINT_ALLOWED_HOSTS=agents.internal,10.0.0.42:9000 ``` A host on its own covers any port on that host; a host with a port pins that port. Matching is exact: no wildcards, no suffixes. An entry written as a URL, or containing `*`, stops startup and names that entry. The list covers agent endpoints only. Browsing is unaffected, the addresses holding a deployment's own cloud credentials are refused whatever is listed, and listing an address permits registering an agent there rather than granting that agent anything. Tenant package agents are declared in the package's own `agents.yaml`, in the directory `TENANT_PACKAGE_DIR` names (`examples/fintech` by default), or each in a file of its own under that package's `agents/` directory, as one of: - `built-in`, with a system prompt; - `remote-ag-ui`, with an endpoint; or - `remote-mastra`, with a Mastra server's address. See [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) and [docs/coworkers.md](docs/coworkers.md). ## Configuration `.env.example` is the source template. A self-hosted Intelligence also needs the license on its own deployment, or it refuses memory; OpenBot logs `intelligence-entitlement-not-ready` at boot when that is missing. More detail: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md). ## API Every OpenBot client uses one API, and its spec is in this repository under [`api/`](api/README.md): - **REST**, in OpenAPI 3.1: [`api/openapi.yaml`](api/openapi.yaml), bundled from one file per area in `api/openapi/`. Every resource is under `/api/v2/organizations/{organizationId}/`, and an installation's one organization is addressed as `default`, so the Bots are at `/api/v2/organizations/default/bots`. - **Live channels**, on WebSockets, in AsyncAPI 3.1: [`api/asyncapi.yaml`](api/asyncapi.yaml). A Bot's run as it streams, what changed in your conversations, a Bot's screen and its terminal. The conventions are the same everywhere. An error is a problem detail (`application/problem+json`, RFC 9457). A list pages with `cursor` and `limit`. Every write takes an `Idempotency-Key` header, and repeating a request with the same key within 24 hours does it once. The web app signs in with its session cookie; anything else sends `Authorization: Bearer` with an API key, which acts as the person who made it, or with an access token from OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. Both work on `/api/v2` only. A client is given one address, OpenBot's. An Intelligence that runs beside OpenBot is reached there too: on a laptop OpenBot's server carries the Intelligence gateway's socket on its own port, and on a cluster the Ingress or HTTPRoute sends that socket's path straight to Intelligence and everything else to OpenBot. Run from a source checkout, the app keeps the gateway's own port unless `OPENBOT_PUBLIC_URL` is set. [Configuration](docs/configuration.md#required-api-server-variables) has the settings. The web app's client is generated from the spec (`bun run api:generate`, into `app/src/lib/api/generated`), and CI fails a pull request whose spec breaks an existing client. The app's screens are moving onto it area by area, and the earlier `/api/...` addresses are retired as each area moves, so a script should call only `/api/v2`. ## Sign in `.env.example` ships `OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER=true`, which is one administrator and no sign-in: how a fresh clone reaches the product without registering an OAuth client first. Delete that line and configure **any one** of Google, Microsoft or Okta before anybody else can reach the deployment. With neither, it refuses to start rather than admitting everybody as an administrator. Configure more than one provider and the sign-in screen offers each of them. These four are needed whichever you pick: ```sh BETTER_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:3001 # where OAuth callbacks come back to BETTER_AUTH_SECRET= # openssl rand -base64 32 TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3010 # where the app is served from INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAILS=you@example.com # comma separated ``` Then the provider. Register the redirect URI shown beside it. ```sh # Google — http://localhost:3001/api/auth/callback/google GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID= GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET= # Microsoft — http://localhost:3001/api/auth/callback/microsoft MICROSOFT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID= MICROSOFT_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET= MICROSOFT_OAUTH_TENANT_ID=common # your directory GUID for staff only # Okta — http://localhost:3001/api/auth/callback/okta OKTA_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID= OKTA_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET= OKTA_OAUTH_ISSUER=https://example.okta.com/oauth2/default ``` Restart. Accounts, sessions and roles are stored in the same PostgreSQL database as everything else. A company's own SAML or OpenID Connect provider is registered while the deployment runs, under Admin → Identity providers, and routed by email domain. An OIDC registration needs every host in the provider's discovery document listed in `TRUSTED_ORIGINS`, not only the issuer. - `INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAILS` is required, because it is what grants the first administrator. After that `/admin/people` can promote others, but an address named here stays an administrator and cannot be demoted or removed from that screen. It is re-read on every sign-in, so editing it takes effect the next time that person signs in. - `MICROSOFT_OAUTH_TENANT_ID` defaults to `common`, which admits personal Microsoft accounts as well as work ones. On a multi-tenant app registration Entra may send no `email` claim at all, so OpenBot falls back to `upn` and then `preferred_username`. If none of the three arrives the sign-in is refused and the reason is logged: add `email` as an optional claim, or use your directory GUID here. - A half-configured provider is refused at start-up rather than at somebody's first attempt to sign in: a client id with no secret, a `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` shorter than 32 characters, or an Okta issuer with no credentials behind it. - **SAML and OIDC** are registered while the deployment runs rather than configured here. Sign in as an administrator and go to Admin → Identity providers with the metadata your identity team gave you. People then sign in by typing their email address, and the domain decides which provider they are sent to. - **Put TLS in front of any deployment.** A page served over plain `http://` on anything but localhost is not a secure context, and sign-in cookies want `Secure`. ### Organization sign-in through another OpenBot A team deployment can leave sign-in to another OpenBot, the authority, configured with the Google, Microsoft or Okta settings above (your Kubernetes OpenBot can serve this role). Set `OPENBOT_ORGANIZATION_AUTH_URL=https://openbot.company.example` to the authority's origin. Use an HTTPS origin; HTTP is accepted only on loopback for local tests. Provider client secrets stay on that authority. The authority verifies the person and their current role; organization mode never substitutes `dev@openbot.local`, and it decides sign-in ahead of `OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER`. This optional URL is separate from `INTELLIGENCE_API_URL`, `INTELLIGENCE_GATEWAY_WS_URL` and `CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY`. Each deployment keeps its own Intelligence project credential. OpenBot Desktop does not offer organization sign-in. It installs the personal edition, which refuses `OPENBOT_ORGANIZATION_AUTH_URL`, and removes that setting from its `.env` on every Start. ## Keeping it to your machine - `agent-computer` drives a browser holding real logins. `docker-compose.yml` binds it to loopback; leave it there. - Store credentials through `/admin/credentials`, which encrypts them. Do not put credential values in tenant YAML or in committed files. - `AGENT_COMPUTER_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS` lets a Bot reach services on this machine. It ships commented out in `.env.example`, is for a laptop only, and a deployment running with `NODE_ENV=production` refuses to start while it is set. - To reach an agent on your own network from a deployment, list its address in `AGENT_ENDPOINT_ALLOWED_HOSTS` instead. That permits the one address, where the switch above permits the network. ## Development ```sh bun run format:check bun run lint bun run typecheck bun run test bun run build ``` After changing the API spec under `api/openapi/`, bundle it and regenerate the app's client, and commit both ([api/README.md](api/README.md)): ```sh bun run api:generate ``` Use `bash scripts/start.sh` for the whole stack and `bash scripts/stop.sh` to take it down. Use `bun run dev` only when you want the app on its own, against a server that is already running. The database schema and its migrations come with the server image, which applies them as it starts. ## Project status [![CI](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openbot/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openbot/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![security](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openbot/actions/workflows/security_zizmor.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openbot/actions/workflows/security_zizmor.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE) [![Latest OpenBot release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CopilotKit/OpenBot?label=release&color=blue)](https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot/releases/latest) ## Documentation - [open.bot](https://open.bot) - [docs/how-openbot-works.md](docs/how-openbot-works.md): a Bot's eight things, and where you set each one - [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) - [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) - [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) - [docs/personal-edition.md](docs/personal-edition.md): OpenBot for one person, with no sign-in and no Admin - [docs/development.md](docs/development.md) - [api/README.md](api/README.md): the API's spec, and how to change it - [docs/coworkers.md](docs/coworkers.md) - [docs/routines.md](docs/routines.md) - [docs/automatic-learning.md](docs/automatic-learning.md) - [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md) - The Helm chart, published with each release: `helm show readme` on it is the Helm guide - [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md) - [docs/web-research.md](docs/web-research.md): public-web search and extraction through Parallel, Exa or Firecrawl ## Contributing - Open an issue or coordinate before starting substantial work. - Keep changes focused and update docs when setup, configuration, architecture, or user behavior changes. - Keep secrets, service-account JSON, customer data, and local transcripts out of the repository. - Run the checks in [Development](#development) before opening a pull request. ## License The OpenBot application source is [MIT-licensed](./LICENSE) © CopilotKit. CopilotKit Intelligence is separately licensed. OpenBot for Business includes Intelligence for use with OpenBot. See [plans and pricing](https://open.bot/pricing).

# 云析 · YunX **粘贴分享链接，直接高速下载 —— 一个开源的 Android 网盘 / 视频解析下载应用** 识别夸克 / UC / 迅雷 / 百度 / 139 / 123 / 115 / 光鸭 / 蓝奏云 / 蓝奏云优享版 的分享链接并自动匹配提取码；也能解析抖音 / 小红书 / 快手 / 微博 / AcFun / 哔哩哔哩 / Pixiv 的视频与图集。Range 分片并发 + 断点续传，图片 / 视频 / 音频可在线预览。 [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CYQawa/YunX?style=flat-square\&label=release\&color=4C8BF5)](https://github.com/CYQawa/YunX/releases/latest) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/CYQawa/YunX?style=flat-square\&logo=github\&color=4C8BF5)](https://github.com/CYQawa/YunX/stargazers) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blue?style=flat-square)](./LICENSE) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Android-3DDC84?style=flat-square\&logo=android\&logoColor=white)](#构建) [![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-7F52FF?style=flat-square\&logo=kotlin\&logoColor=white)](https://kotlinlang.org/) [![Compose](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jetpack%20Compose-MD3Expressive-4285F4?style=flat-square\&logo=jetpackcompose\&logoColor=white)](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/compose) [下载最新版](https://github.com/CYQawa/YunX/releases/latest) · [功能](#功能) · [使用](#使用) · [构建](#构建) · [常见问题](#常见问题) [![QQ交流群](https://img.shields.io/badge/QQ%E7%BE%A4-635207650-12B7F5?style=flat-square\&logo=qq\&logoColor=white)](http://qm.qq.com/cgi-bin/qm/qr?...\&group_code=635207650)
*** > **云析永远免费开源。** 如果你是在任何地方"花钱买到"的，说明你被骗了，请立即退款。 > 任何收费版本均为二次打包的诈骗版本，与本项目无关。 > **云析使用AGPL-3.0开源协议** 如果你使用了云析的代码，未经授权请遵守协议，同样以AGPL-3.0开放源代码 > 本仓库为 Android 端 App；官方 PC 端见 [YunX-Desktop](https://github.com/tidain/YunX-Desktop) ## 截图 |
|
|
| | :-----------------------: | :-------------------------: | :--------------------------: | | ![解析输入](images/Link.jpg) | ![文件列表](images/Parsing.jpg) | ![下载管理](images/Download.jpg) | | 解析直链 | 分享解析 | 下载管理 | | ![网盘登录](images/Login.jpg) | ![设置](images/Setting.jpg) | ![关于](images/about.jpg) | | 网盘登录 | 设置 | 关于 | ## 功能 - **网盘分享链接解析** —— 识别夸克 / UC / 迅雷 / 百度 / 139 / 123 / 115 / 光鸭 / 蓝奏云 / 蓝奏云优享版 的分享链接，自动匹配提取码 - **视频链接解析** —— 粘贴抖音 / 快手 / 微博 / AcFun 的分享链接免登录直出直链；小红书需登录后解析；哔哩哔哩登录后画质更高，Pixiv 未登录只能拿到部分公开作品、在「账号」页粘贴浏览器 Cookie 后可解析全部作品（含 R18 与受限作品），哔哩哔哩的音视频分轨由应用内部合轨（不依赖 ffmpeg） - **高速下载** —— Range 分片并发 + 断点续传，任务保存请求头与固定分片规划，并发上限 32 - **在线预览与播放** —— 图片 / 视频 / 音频直接在线播放（逐请求带上 Referer / Cookie，直链不再 403）；网盘里的常见文本文件也能在线打开 - **图集两列网格** —— 图文笔记直接把图铺成两列，点开可翻页 / 双指放大 / 单张下载，长按进入多选批量下载 - **下载自动归组** —— 整个文件夹、或一次批量下载的图片，在下载页收纳成一个可折叠分组 - **临时转存清理** —— 百度 / 迅雷 / 光鸭取链后清理；夸克保留到下载完成或删除任务后清理 - **多平台登录** —— 夸克 / UC / 百度 / 139 / 115 使用 WebView Cookie；迅雷 / 光鸭 使用账号密码 / 短信验证码；123 使用账号密码换取 JWT；蓝奏云 / 蓝奏云优享版 使用账号密码 - **认证备份** —— 使用用户口令派生密钥，以 AES-GCM 加密 Cookie / JWT 备份文件 - **凭证存储** —— 账号 Cookie / JWT、GitHub Token 和下载请求头保存在应用私有数据中；导出的认证备份文件使用用户口令派生的密钥进行 AES-GCM 加密 - **剪贴板识别** —— 复制分享链接后回到应用，提示一键粘贴解析 ## 支持平台 **网盘** - 夸克网盘 - UC 网盘 - 迅雷网盘 - 百度网盘 - 123 云盘 - 139 网盘（和彩云） - 115 网盘 - 光鸭云盘 - 蓝奏云 - 蓝奏云优享版 **视频 / 图集** - 抖音 - 小红书 - 快手 - 微博 - AcFun - 哔哩哔哩（需登录才能解析高清） - Pixiv（未登录只能拿到部分公开作品；不支持网页登录，可在「账号」页粘贴浏览器 Cookie 以解析全部作品） > \[!WARNING] > **不建议使用百度网盘，可能导致账号被风控！** > \[!NOTE] > 其他网盘与视频平台暂未支持，如有需要请开一个 [issue](https://github.com/CYQawa/YunX/issues)。 ## 使用 1. 在「账号」页登录需要使用的网盘账号（需要登录的视频平台也在这里登录） 2. 在「解析」页粘贴链接（可带提取码）：分享链接解析网盘，视频链接会自动识别平台 3. 网盘链接浏览分享内容、点击文件获取下载直链；视频链接在结果页直接预览或下载，图片笔记长按可多选 4. 在「下载」页查看进度，支持暂停 / 继续 / 删除 / 打开 ## 技术栈 | 分类 | 选型 | | ----- | -------------------------------------------- | | 语言 | Kotlin | | UI | Jetpack Compose + Material 3 | | 持久化 | Room（KSP 注解处理）+ SharedPreferences | | 网络 | OkHttp 4.12.0（请求 + 分片下载） | | 预览播放 | Media3 ExoPlayer / Coil 3 | | 音视频合轨 | MediaExtractor + MediaMuxer（系统原生，逐样本重封装不重编码） | | 构建 | Gradle + KSP | ## 构建 要求：minSdk 24，targetSdk 34。 ```bash git clone https://github.com/CYQawa/YunX.git ``` 用 Android Studio 打开项目直接构建即可。项目在 AndroidIDE 上开发调试，理论上也兼容其它 Android 构建环境。 ## 友情推荐 > [文析助手](https://github.com/z7786/wenxi)(提供了部分接口) ## 常见问题
百度网盘下载/转存不了？ 你的账号被风控了，见[issue #9](https://github.com/CYQawa/YunX/issues/9)
有PC端吗？ 有。官方 PC 端由协作者 雑魚（[tidain](https://github.com/tidain)）开发维护：[YunX-Desktop](https://github.com/tidain/YunX-Desktop) 由于作者没有电脑、无法开发 PC 端，**PC 端的开发与维护由 雑魚 独立负责，作者不参与**；PC 端相关的功能与问题请到对应仓库反馈。

# ggml
Tensor library for machine learning [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/ggml-org/ggml?filter=v*)](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases) [![CI](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/actions/workflows/build-cpu.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/actions/workflows/build-cpu.yml)
## Quick start Build from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml cd ggml mkdir build && cd build cmake .. cmake --build . --config Release -j 8 ``` For a minimal, fully commented example (matrix multiplication), see [examples/simple](examples/simple). ## Description The main goal of `ggml` is to be a simple, portable, and efficient tensor library for machine learning with minimal setup. - Plain C/C++ implementation without any dependencies - Cross-platform - x86, ARM, RISC-V, LoongArch, PowerPC, s390x, and WebAssembly - SIMD-optimized kernels for x86, ARM, and RISC-V - Broad backend support - CPU, GPU, NPU, and browser - 2- to 8-bit integer quantization, plus MXFP4 and NVFP4 microscaling formats - Zero memory allocations during runtime ## Documentation - [The GGUF file format](docs/gguf.md) - [Introduction to ggml](https://huggingface.co/blog/introduction-to-ggml) - [GGML tips & tricks](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/wiki/GGML-Tips-&-Tricks) ## Contributing - For changes to the core `ggml` library (including to the CMake build system), please open a PR in [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) - doing so will make your PR more visible, better tested, and more likely to be reviewed

repositories.name: container
repositories.description: A tool for creating and running Linux containers using lightweight virtual machines on a Mac. It is written in Swift, and optimized for Apple silicon.
repositories.readme:
container

`container` is a tool that you can use to create and run Linux containers as lightweight virtual machines on your Mac. It's written in Swift, and optimized for Apple silicon. The tool consumes and produces [OCI-compatible container images](https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec), so you can pull and run images from any standard container registry. You can push images that you build to those registries as well, and run the images in any other OCI-compatible application. `container` uses the [Containerization](https://github.com/apple/containerization) Swift package for low-level container, image, and process management. ## Get started ### Requirements You need a Mac with Apple silicon to run `container`. To build it, see the [BUILDING](./BUILDING.md) document. `container` is designed to run on macOS 26 or later, since it takes advantage of new features and enhancements to virtualization and networking in this release. We do not support older versions of macOS and the `container` maintainers typically will not address issues that cannot be reproduced on macOS 26 or later. ### Initial install Download the latest signed installer package for `container` from the [GitHub release page](https://github.com/apple/container/releases). To install the tool, double-click the package file and follow the instructions. Enter your administrator password when prompted, to give the installer permission to place the installed files under `/usr/local`. Start the system service with: ```bash container system start ``` ### Run your first container ```bash container run --rm alpine echo hello ``` This pulls the `alpine` image, runs it in a lightweight Linux VM, prints `hello`, and removes the container when it exits. See the [tutorial](./docs/tutorials/start-here.md) for a fuller walkthrough that builds and publishes an image of your own. ### Upgrade or downgrade For both upgrading and downgrading, you can manually download and install the signed installer package by following the steps from [initial install](#initial-install) or use the `update-container.sh` script (installed to `/usr/local/bin`). If you're upgrading or downgrading, you must stop your existing `container`: ```bash container system stop ``` To upgrade to the latest release, simply run the command below: ```bash /usr/local/bin/update-container.sh ``` To downgrade, you must uninstall your existing `container` (the `-k` flag keeps your user data, while `-d` removes it): ```bash /usr/local/bin/uninstall-container.sh -k /usr/local/bin/update-container.sh -v 0.3.0 ``` Start the system service with: ```bash container system start ``` ### Uninstall Use the `uninstall-container.sh` script (installed to `/usr/local/bin`) to remove `container` from your system. To remove your user data along with the tool, run: ```bash /usr/local/bin/uninstall-container.sh -d ``` To retain your user data so that it is available should you reinstall later, run: ```bash /usr/local/bin/uninstall-container.sh -k ``` ## Next steps - Take [a guided tour of `container`](./docs/tutorials/start-here.md) by building, running, and publishing a simple web server image. - Learn how to [use various `container` features](./docs/how-to.md). - Explore the [container-examples repo](https://github.com/apple/container-examples/) that contains examples that show you how to work with `container`, such as [developing Linux apps in a container machine with Visual Studio Code](https://github.com/apple/container-examples/tree/main/container-machine-vscode) and [running a three-tier app on a container cluster behind a gateway](https://github.com/apple/container-examples/tree/main/container-cluster-gateway). - Read a brief description and [technical overview](./docs/technical-overview.md) of `container`. - Browse the [full command reference](./docs/command-reference.md). - [Build and run](./BUILDING.md) `container` on your own development system. - View the project [API documentation](https://apple.github.io/container/documentation/). ## Contributing Contributions to `container` are welcome and encouraged. Please see our [main contributing guide](https://github.com/apple/containerization/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information. ## Project Status The container project is under active development. Its release versions are product versions, not semantic versions. The `container` CLI compatibility generally preserves backward compatibility within a major release (not breaking existing scripts), however, there may be the odd case where breaking compatibility may be necessary. **Note:** Features marked *experimental* (for example, the `cluster` subcommand) may change and do not guarantee backward compatibility. The `container-apiserver` XPC API compatibility preserves forward and backward compatibility within a major version. Other non-public XPC helpers do not guarantee CLI or API compatibility across different versions. The `container` application data provides forward compatibility only, guaranteed within one major version. Upgrading to a newer major version may require a specific upgrade path.

# goose _your native open source AI agent — desktop app, CLI, and API — for code, workflows, and everything in between_

goose is a general-purpose AI agent that runs on your machine. Not just for code — use it for research, writing, automation, data analysis, or anything you need to get done. [Try Qwen Code 1.0 Preview](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/v1.0.0-preview) · [Documentation](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/1.x/) · [中文文档](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/1.x/zh/users/overview/). | ## Why Qwen Code? - **Agentic out of the box** — Auto-Memory, Skills, SubAgents, and MCP work from the first session. Agent Teams, Agent Arena, and Dynamic Workflows are built in too — experimental or opt-in, as noted in [Capabilities](#capabilities). - **Open-source, inside and out** — The framework and the Qwen models are open-source. They evolve together. No vendor lock-in. - **Multi-protocol** — Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs. Any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime. - **Beyond the terminal** — IDE plugins, Desktop app, Web UI, SDKs, and chat integrations (Telegram / DingTalk / WeChat / WeCom / Feishu and more). > [!TIP] > Qwen Code is actively iterating on itself — using its own agent and models to file issues, submit PRs, review code, and run tests. Powered by the community, driven by AI. ## Installation Looking for **Qwen Code 1.0 Preview**? [Get started here](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/v1.0.0-preview). The instructions below are for the main version. **Linux / macOS:** ```bash curl -fsSL https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.sh | bash ``` **Windows:** ```powershell irm https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.ps1 | iex ``` > Restart your terminal after installation to ensure environment variables take effect.
NPM / Homebrew **NPM** (requires [Node.js 22+](https://nodejs.org/)): ```bash npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code@latest ``` **Homebrew** (macOS / Linux): ```bash brew install qwen-code ```
## Quick Start Open a terminal in your project and start Qwen Code: ```bash cd /path/to/your-project qwen ``` Inside the session, run `/auth` and choose [**Qwen Account with Subscription**](https://chat.qwen.ai/?memberPlan=qwen_code&entry=qwen_code&paywallScene=cli) to sign in with your **Plus or Pro subscription**, or configure a provider with an API key. Then try: ```text Explain this repository and show me where to start. ``` See the [Authentication Guide](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/auth/) and [Settings Reference](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/settings/) for detailed setup.
See the terminal interface ![Qwen Code terminal interface](https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i2/O1CN01K0nwj41RM1Il8kB0t_!!6000000002096-2-tps-1544-1060.png)
## How to Use Qwen Code Choose the interface that fits your workflow: | Interface | Get started | | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Terminal** | Run `qwen` in your project — see [Quick Start](#quick-start). | | **Desktop** | [Download Qwen Code Desktop](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/releases/tag/desktop-latest) for macOS, Windows, and Linux. | | **Web** | Run `qwen serve --open` to open the [Web UI](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/qwen-serve/) in your browser. _(experimental)_ | | **Editor** | Set up [VS Code](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-vscode/), [Zed](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-zed/), or [JetBrains](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-jetbrains/). | | **Chat** | Connect [Telegram](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/telegram/), [DingTalk](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/dingtalk/), [WeChat](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/weixin/), [WeCom](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/wecom/), [Feishu](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/feishu/), [QQ Bot](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/qqbot/), [Email](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/email/), or [GitHub](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/github/), then run `qwen channel start`. See the [Channels overview](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/overview/) for webhook senders and plugin adapters. | For automation and custom integrations: - **Headless** — Run `qwen -p "..."` in scripts, CI/CD, or batch jobs. - **SDKs** — Build with [TypeScript](./packages/sdk-typescript/README.md), [Python](./packages/sdk-python/README.md), or [Java](./packages/sdk-java/qwencode/README.md). - **Daemon** — Run `qwen serve` to connect clients over HTTP + SSE (ACP). _(experimental)_ [Daemon guide](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/qwen-serve/). - **Computer Use** — Set up [native MCP tools](./packages/cua-driver/README.md#agent-integration) or [Node REPL + SDK](./packages/node-repl/README.md#usage) in Qwen Code, Claude Code, or Codex.
SDK example (Python) ```python import asyncio from qwen_code_sdk import is_sdk_result_message, query async def main() -> None: result = query( "Summarize the repository layout.", { "cwd": "/path/to/project", "path_to_qwen_executable": "qwen", }, ) async for message in result: if is_sdk_result_message(message): print(message["result"]) asyncio.run(main()) ```
## Daemon Mode Run Qwen Code as a long-lived service when you want browser, editor, SDK, and automation clients to share agent sessions without each starting a separate process. The daemon provides the built-in Web Shell and an HTTP + SSE API, supports multiple workspaces, and lets clients reconnect to active sessions. Start it in the foreground and open the Web Shell: ```bash qwen serve --open ``` The default address is `http://127.0.0.1:4170`. To run and manage it in the background instead: ```bash qwen daemon start qwen daemon status qwen daemon logs -f qwen daemon stop ``` By default, the daemon listens on loopback without bearer authentication; any local process that can reach it can use the full API, including code execution. On shared or untrusted hosts, set `QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN` and use `--require-auth`. See the [Daemon guide](./docs/users/qwen-serve.md) for workspaces, authentication, remote access, and the API. ## Capabilities Qwen Code ships with a complete agent harness — multi-agent orchestration, persistent memory, and deep extensibility, all built in. ### Agentic core - **[SubAgents](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/sub-agents/)** — delegate focused subtasks to specialized agents with their own context and toolsets, in the foreground or background. - **[Agent Teams](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/multi-agent-coordination/)** _(experimental)_ — a leader coordinates teammates that share a task list and exchange messages, with read-only investigators and an optional single worktree writer. - **[Agent Arena](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/arena/)** _(experimental)_ — run the same task on multiple models in isolated Git worktrees, compare solutions side by side, and merge the winner. - **[Dynamic Workflows](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/workflow-mode/)** _(opt-in)_ — the model writes JavaScript workflows that orchestrate agents: parallel fan-out, verification passes, and resumable runs. - **[Goals](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/goals/)** — `/goal` keeps the session working across turns until an independent verifier accepts the outcome, within a token budget. - **[Scheduled tasks](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/scheduled-tasks/)** — `/loop` and cron tools re-run prompts on an interval or at a set time. ### Memory, skills, and sessions - **[Auto-Memory](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/memory/)** — the agent writes its own notes and recalls them across sessions; your `QWEN.md` and `AGENTS.md` briefings load automatically. - **[Skills & Auto-Skills](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/skills/)** — built-in skills (`/review`, `/batch`, `/bugfix`…) work out of the box; `/learn` distills docs or code into new skills, the agent can generate skills on its own _(opt-in)_, and `/curator` maintains the library. - **[Session management](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/session-overview/)** — resume past conversations with [`/resume`](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/commands/), and browse, rename, or archive sessions. ### Extensibility and control - **[Hooks](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/hooks/)** — run your own scripts at lifecycle events: before and after tool calls, session start and end, and more. - **[MCP](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/mcp/)** — connect any Model Context Protocol server to add tools, resources, and prompts. - **[LSP integration](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/lsp/)** _(experimental, opt-in)_ — native language-server support: go-to-definition, references, diagnostics, and code actions. - **[Computer Use & Browser Use](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/computer-use/)** — automate desktop applications and the browser through native MCP tools. - **[Plan Mode & approval modes](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/approval-mode/)** — plan read-only before touching files, then choose per-call confirmation, auto-edit, classifier-driven [Auto Mode](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/auto-mode/), or YOLO. - **[Sandbox](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/sandbox/) & [Git worktrees](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/worktree/)** — confine tool execution with built-in sandboxing and isolate wide-ranging edits in a temporary worktree. ### Open and multi-platform - **Open framework and models** — the framework and the Qwen models are open source and evolve together. - **[Any provider](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/model-providers/)** — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs, plus any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime. - **Every interface** — IDE plugins, desktop app, Web UI, IM channels, headless mode, SDKs, and daemon mode. See [How to Use Qwen Code](#how-to-use-qwen-code). ## Qwen Code Evaluation On **SWE-bench Verified**, seven Qwen Code versions scored **76.40%–77.80%** on average using the same Qwen 3.7 Max model (500 tasks, three trials per version). ![Average SWE-bench Verified scores by Qwen Code version: 0.0.14, 77.80%; 0.1.0, 76.73%; 0.5.0, 76.60%; 0.10.0, 76.47%; 0.15.0, 77.67%; 0.19.0, 76.40%; 0.22.0, 77.33%.](./.github/assets/qwen-code-avg-score-trend.svg) [Full results and evaluation configuration →](./docs/evaluation.md) ## Ecosystem - [**Qwen Code Desktop**](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/releases/tag/desktop-latest) — Official desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux - [**AionUi**](https://github.com/iOfficeAI/AionUi) — A modern GUI for command-line AI tools including Qwen Code - [**Gemini CLI Desktop**](https://github.com/Piebald-AI/gemini-cli-desktop) — A cross-platform desktop/web/mobile UI for Qwen Code - [**qwen-audio-agent**](https://github.com/QwenAudio/qwen-audio-agent) — Realtime full-duplex voice frontend for Qwen Code over ACP — talk hands-free with barge-in and a local wake word - [**🦞 Qwen Code Claw**](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx) — Let other agents (Claude, Codex, etc.) delegate coding tasks to Qwen Code via ACP. Paste this prompt into your agent: ```text Use Qwen Code as a coding agent. First, fetch and read this skill reference: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/refs/heads/main/.qwen/skills/qwen-code-claw/SKILL.md Then follow the instructions inside to install, authenticate, and use Qwen Code via acpx for all coding tasks. ``` - [**Aliyun Model Studio CLI**](https://github.com/modelstudioai/cli) — Official CLI for Aliyun's AI platform (`bailian-cli`). Extends Qwen Code with image/video generation, knowledge retrieval, app orchestration, and model deployment ## Privacy See the [Terms of Service and Privacy Notice](./docs/users/support/tos-privacy.md), including [Chrome extension and Browser Use data handling](./docs/users/support/tos-privacy.md#chrome-extension-and-browser-use). ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines. ## Acknowledgments This project was originally based on [Google Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) v0.8.2. We gratefully acknowledge the Gemini CLI team's excellent work. Starting from Qwen Code v0.1, we stopped syncing with upstream and began independent development as a multi-protocol, multi-platform agent framework with deep integrations for Qwen models and beyond.

repositories.name: Orion-Store
repositories.description: The ultimate home for Open Source and Cleaned apps. OrionStore offers instant access to YouTube Morphe, YT Music Morphe, and essential open-source tools without the clutter. No servers, no tracking, just a beautiful, modern gateway to the apps you love.
repositories.readme:
A transparent app store built around public releases, inspectable metadata, and automation you can actually follow.
Now fully native.

  


Sources Supported


🔍 Orion does not have any trackers! Saw a few people asking about "trackers" flagged in App Manager or TrackerControl, so wanted to clear up what those actually are. **What they actually are:** - Scanners flag library components by name, not active surveillance. - Everything flagged comes from one library, the Unity Ads SDK behind the optional "Fuel the Code" quest. - Since 2.4.5 Orion strips everything from it that Fuel the Code does not need: its app-start hook, its background service, and the advertising ID and ad-measurement permissions. What is left is **`FullScreenWebViewDisplay`**, the screen that plays the video you chose to watch. **How it works in Orion:** - Unity only starts when you tap to watch a rewarded video in "Fuel the Code" for XP. It never runs at app start. - There are zero background services, no banner ads, and no advertising ID. Orion collects and sends no user data. - If you do not care about the rewarded XP quest, you can block it right there in App Manager. The store will still work completely fine.

## Orion Store 2.0 · Native at last Orion Store has been **rebuilt from the ground up as a native Android app**. The web app has been rewritten in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose on **Material 3 Expressive**, with spring motion, shape morphing, a new storefront and features that were never possible before. Updating from 1.x is a normal install over the old app, and your profile, XP, badges, favorites and settings come along. Read the full [2.0.0 release notes](RELEASE_NOTES_2.0.0.md).

## Overview Orion Store is an Android-first store client that leans on public sources instead of hiding everything behind a private service layer. The app pulls catalog data from public JSON, resolves releases from GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg, and keeps the delivery path understandable enough that users can see where things come from and how updates are discovered. This repository is the client application itself. The live catalog, configuration, notices, and release metadata used by the app are maintained separately in [RookieEnough/Orion-Data](https://github.com/RookieEnough/Orion-Data), which keeps the UI and the store data cleanly separated. > Orion is built for people who care where software comes from, not just how quickly it downloads. At a glance: - Public JSON catalog with inspectable configuration - Multi-source releases (GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg) - Native install, update, and security tooling - Skip Android's 24-hour unverified-app wait with built-in wireless install ### Orbit and Obtainium Orbit follows an app from the page it is published on and installs the file that page offers. Following a source that way is the same idea as [Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium) by Imran Remtulla. Orion is a separate app. It does not include Obtainium's code. The Obtainium name is used so an Obtainium export, an `obtainium://` link, or the public Obtainium apps directory can be brought into Orbit.

## What makes Orion different The point of Orion is not to pretend infrastructure does not exist. It is to reduce hidden infrastructure and move as much of the important behavior as possible into public, inspectable layers. Catalog entries are plain data. Release sources stay visible. Automation is handled through workflows and workers that can be reviewed, rather than through a black-box backend that users have to trust on faith. That design carries through the app. Orion tracks installed packages, surfaces updates, manages download state, installs natively, and exposes developer-facing diagnostics for people who want to see what the store is actually doing under the hood.

## Feature atlas

Release intelligence
Orion reads public metadata, resolves upstream releases, and keeps source provenance visible instead of burying it behind a store-owned backend. It reads your device architecture and recommends the right APK.

Public JSON Mirrors Multi-source parsing ABI detection
Update center
A native download engine with live notifications, a persistent queue, batch updates, and per-app ignore rules you can undo from My Apps.

Foreground downloads Queue Ignored updates

Native install flow
System installer, a specific installer, Shizuku silent installs, or the built-in wireless ADB installer that skips Android's 24-hour wait for unverified apps. Set it up once through a guided notification.

Wireless ADB Shizuku Installer choice
Sentinel security
Security tooling is built into the product: malware scans for installed apps and VirusTotal checks for any APK before it is installed.

Sentinel VirusTotal Threat database

Guardian power tools
Revoke risky permissions, pull the APK out of any app, and remove or restore system apps without root, rated by the Universal Android Debloater database.

Permissions APK extraction Debloater
Developer visibility
Mirror source, cache state, GitHub API quota, package detective, raw metadata explorer and source switching, all in Settings › Developer.

Developer mode Diagnostics Metadata inspection

Orion AI
Describe the app you need and Orion AI finds it in the catalog, or ask how any Orion feature works. Bring your own Gemini, ChatGPT or Claude key, or run a model right on the phone, offline.

Streaming chat On-device models One-tap installs
Palettes, your way
Fourteen tuned palettes plus a palette maker: pick a seed color, a style and preview every tone in Light, Dusk, Dark and OLED before you save it.

Material You Palette maker Four themes

Orbit
Follow any app from the page it is published on. Paste a repo, a store page or a direct file, and Orion installs it and checks for updates the same way it does for the catalog.

Your sources Obtainium import Tokens
Open the file you have
Install with Orion opens an APK, XAPK, APKM, APKS or a zip of APKs from a file manager. A bundle is read from the APKs inside it, and only the pieces for this phone are installed.

XAPK APKM APKS
### And a lot more - **Material 3 Expressive design:** expressive springs, shape morphs, wavy progress, icon hand-off animations, and Material You colors. - **A real level system:** every ad, download, submission and Dino Run earns XP. Pilot cards turn Bronze, Silver and Gold, and you can flip yours to sign it. - **Fuel the Code:** a story-driven support quest, now in Chapter 2 · The Forkening, with bosses and badges to earn. - **Community:** submit apps straight from a GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg repo, build custom bundles, and climb the leaderboard. - **Personalization:** light, dark, dusk and OLED themes, custom fonts, pixel pull-to-refresh characters, layouts and visible tabs.

## Official developer badges If you are a developer, you can promote that your application is hosted on Orion Store by adding our official badge to your repository's readme or your product website.

### How to Get Your Badge Integration Link: 1. **Submit Your App**: Submit your application to the Orion Store via this client or our repository submission form. 2. **Enable Developer Mode**: Once approved and live in the store, open Orion Store and tap the **Orion Store** title in the header 7 times to unlock Developer Mode. 3. **Copy Integration Code**: Open your app's detail page, expand **Developer Deep Links**, and copy the **Markdown Badge** for your repository's README or the **HTML Badge** for your website.

## How the project is structured Orion Store 2.0 is a single-activity Jetpack Compose app in MVVM style. A tour of the code lives in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).
Area Responsibility
app/src/main/java/com/orion/store/ui/ Compose screens, the theme and motion system, and MainViewModel, which orchestrates loading, downloads, installs and overlays
app/src/main/java/com/orion/store/data/ Catalog processing, persisted settings and data stores, version logic, XP and levels
app/src/main/java/com/orion/store/platform/ Package tracking, the download service, Shizuku and wireless ADB installs, VirusTotal, and the 1.x data carry-over
tools/ Generators for the Material Symbols icon set and the color schemes
Orion Legacy/ The original React + Capacitor web app (1.x), kept for reference and for the web build

## Building You need **JDK 21** (the JetBrains Runtime bundled with Android Studio works) and the Android SDK. ```bash ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug # debug APK ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest # logic tests ``` Release builds read the signing key from a local `keystore.properties` (never committed): ```properties storeFile=/path/to/your.keystore keyAlias=your-alias storePassword=... keyPassword=... ``` ```bash ./gradlew :app:assembleRelease ``` Or open the project folder in Android Studio and run the `app` configuration on a device. ### Legacy web app The 1.x web app lives in [`Orion Legacy/`](Orion%20Legacy) and still builds as before: ```bash cd "Orion Legacy" npm install npm run dev ```

## Data, workers and automation Orion is best understood as backend-light rather than backend-free. The catalog and remote configuration are public, but the project still uses a few narrow pieces of infrastructure where they make sense: Cloudflare worker code for leaderboard relay, image proxying, delta aggregation, submission handling and Sentinel support lives in `Orion Legacy/workers/`, and automation runs through GitHub Actions here and in Orion-Data. That split is intentional. The app stays focused on the client, while the data and automation layers remain separately inspectable.

## Contributing Contributions are welcome, especially in the areas that matter most to a store client: installer reliability, release resolution, UI polish, Android behavior, security tooling, and documentation. If you are changing catalog entries or store metadata, that work usually belongs in the data repository or the submission flow rather than in this client codebase. Start with [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md), then `ui/MainViewModel.kt`, `data/CatalogProcessor.kt` and `platform/AppTracker.kt` for how the store loads data, resolves releases and installs apps.

## Community The project lives across a few public surfaces: - `Website`: [orionstore.pages.dev](https://orionstore.pages.dev) - `Orion-Data`: [github.com/RookieEnough/Orion-Data](https://github.com/RookieEnough/Orion-Data) - `Discord`: [discord.com/invite/CrM6y4ujnq](https://discord.com/invite/CrM6y4ujnq) - `Ko-fi`: [ko-fi.com/rookie_z](https://ko-fi.com/rookie_z) - `PayPal`: [paypal.me/RookieEnough](https://paypal.me/RookieEnough) - `UPI ID`: `rookiez@ptyes`

## Credits - **[Install with Options](https://github.com/zacharee/InstallWithOptions)** by Zachary Wander (MIT): Orion's "Install with options" sheet is inspired by its set of install options. Orion's version is its own implementation on top of `pm install`. - **[Dhizuku](https://github.com/iamr0s/Dhizuku)** and the **[Dhizuku API](https://github.com/iamr0s/Dhizuku-API)** by iamr0s (MIT): device owner installs and uninstalls. - **[Shizuku](https://github.com/RikkaApps/Shizuku)** by RikkaApps: silent installs and the Guardian tools. - **[Universal Android Debloater Next Generation](https://github.com/Universal-Debloater-Alliance/universal-android-debloater-next-generation)**: the package notes and removal ratings behind Debloat.

Made with 💜 by RookieZ

repositories.readme:
# Tailscale

https://tailscale.com

Private WireGuard® networks made easy

## Overview

This repository contains the majority of Tailscale's open source code.
Notably, it includes the `tailscaled` daemon and
the `tailscale` CLI tool. The `tailscaled` daemon runs on Linux, Windows,
[macOS](https://tailscale.com/kb/1065/macos-variants/), and to varying degrees
on FreeBSD and OpenBSD. The Tailscale iOS and Android apps use this repo's
code, but this repo doesn't contain the mobile GUI code.

Other [Tailscale repos](https://github.com/orgs/tailscale/repositories) of note:

* the Android app is at https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-android
* the Synology package is at https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-synology
* the QNAP package is at https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-qpkg
* the Chocolatey packaging is at https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-chocolatey

For background on which parts of Tailscale are open source and why,
see [https://tailscale.com/opensource/](https://tailscale.com/opensource/).

## Using

We serve packages for a variety of distros and platforms at
[https://pkgs.tailscale.com](https://pkgs.tailscale.com/).

## Other clients

The [macOS, iOS, and Windows clients](https://tailscale.com/download)
use the code in this repository but additionally include small GUI
wrappers. The GUI wrappers on non-open source platforms are themselves
not open source.

## Building

We always require the latest Go release, currently Go 1.27. (While we build
releases with our [Go fork](https://github.com/tailscale/go/), its use is not
required.)

```
go install tailscale.com/cmd/tailscale{,d}
```

If you're packaging Tailscale for distribution, use `build_dist.sh`
instead, to burn commit IDs and version info into the binaries:

```
./build_dist.sh tailscale.com/cmd/tailscale
./build_dist.sh tailscale.com/cmd/tailscaled
```

If your distro has conventions that preclude the use of
`build_dist.sh`, please do the equivalent of what it does in your
distro's way, so that bug reports contain useful version information.

## Bugs

Please file any issues about this code or the hosted service on
[the issue tracker](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues).

## Contributing

PRs welcome! But please file bugs. Commit messages should [reference
bugs](https://docs.github.com/en/github/writing-on-github/autolinked-references-and-urls).

We require [Developer Certificate of
Origin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developer_Certificate_of_Origin)
`Signed-off-by` lines in commits.

See [commit-messages.md](docs/commit-messages.md) (or skim `git log`) for our commit message style.

## About Us

[Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/) is primarily developed by the
people at https://github.com/orgs/tailscale/people. For other contributors,
see:

* https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/graphs/contributors
* https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale-android/graphs/contributors

## Legal

WireGuard is a registered trademark of Jason A. Donenfeld.

repositories.description: Open-source generative UI framework: agents stream layout data, and apps render it with native components in React, Angular, Lit, Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose.
repositories.readme: # A2UI **Build delightful, fast, reliable agentic experiences** A2UI (Agent-to-User Interface) is an open-source generative UI framework, complete with a protocol optimized for streaming dynamic user interfaces at low latency, native renderers for web and mobile frameworks, and agent SDKs in several popular languages. With A2UI, your agents can communicate with your users using natively rendered widgets, in addition to text. _Examples of UI compositions that A2UI can express._ ## Quick links - [Main website](https://a2ui.org). - Try it in your browser using [A2UI Composer](https://a2ui-project.github.io/composer/). - [Supported renderers](https://a2ui.org/reference/renderers/). - [Supported agents](https://a2ui.org/reference/agents/). - [Protocol specification](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/). ## Introduction Large language models (LLMs) and decision models (e.g. [Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/)) excel at creating text and code and at making fast decisions on top of raw structured data (e.g. JSON). A2UI gives these models a specialized vocabulary for expressing user interfaces. A2UI expresses UI using _data_, not code. A schema for the data exchanged between the agent and the renderer enforces strict capability boundaries for the agent, keeping agent-generated experiences safe and aligned with the business requirements of your application. A _core library_, a _native framework adapter_, and a _catalog of components_ provide access to native components and form the building blocks that the agent _composes_ into a final user experience, making the result expressive and high-performance. ## When to use A2UI Use A2UI when any of the following apply to your application: - Parts of your application are agent- and/or server-driven. By design, A2UI supports remote rendering. - You want the UI to be composed dynamically, tailored to the user's immediate need. Instead of making your users navigate through multiple screens to solve their problems, have the agent build the right flow of UI that guides users directly to solutions. - You need the highest performance and visual fidelity. A2UI renders UI using the framework of your choice, typically one that the host app itself is written in. WebViews or HTML are not required. - The same agent streams UI to multiple platforms or frameworks, such as Flutter, React, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose. A2UI helps keep the user experience compatible and consistent across all screens. - The agent is remote, third-party, or operates across a trust boundary. For example, the agent must not be able to handle certain kinds of data (credit card/account numbers, PII, financial data). A2UI helps enforce the trust boundary and protect your app's critical functionality from hallucinations using a strict schema, and by expressing UI using validated data rather than executable code. ## A2UI core philosophy We develop A2UI under the guidance of the following core principles: - **Security first**: The app developer controls what the agent can and cannot do in the app. A2UI provides a framework for specifying and enforcing the necessary guardrails, such as expressing UI as data, validating inputs and outputs against a schema, and disallowing arbitrary executable code. Every capability granted to the agent is either a safe standard capability built into the framework, or a capability explicitly granted by the app developer. - **Model-friendly and server-driven**: The A2UI protocol is designed to be efficiently generated by language and decision models and transported over the network, and to support progressive rendering (or "streaming") for a responsive user experience. An agent can adapt the UI based on where the user takes the conversation. A2UI supports swappable inference formats, so you can tailor inference to specific models and use cases. - **Native rendering and portability**: A2UI renders UI using the framework native to your app, with renderers for many major UI frameworks. No need to change frameworks unless required for other reasons. ## Architecture A2UI's architecture is made of multiple layers spanning the full stack that connects the agent to the application: 1. **Inference**: An agent (typically backed by a language or a decision model) instructed by an A2UI skill (created using an A2UI Agent SDK) generates the description of UI and data using an appropriate inference format (e.g. A2UI Express, or a decision tree). 2. **Transport**: An A2UI Agent SDK, embedded in a larger agent architecture, parses and validates the model's output, expands macros, and converts the UI to the wire-stable _A2UI Transport_ protocol messages, which are sent to the renderer. 3. **Rendering**: A renderer is made of an _A2UI Core_ library (e.g. the `@a2ui/web_core` npm package, or `a2ui_core` Dart package), a UI framework adapter (e.g. `@a2ui/react` React adapter, or `a2ui_flutter` Flutter adapter), and a widget catalog. The core library parses the incoming messages and creates a framework-agnostic in-memory representation of the UI and data. The framework adapter maps the in-memory representation to concrete framework-specific UI widgets. The widget catalog provides access to the widgets the agent is allowed to compose. ## Getting started Pick the path that matches where you want to start: | Path | What you get | Time | | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | | 🍜 **[Quickstart](https://a2ui.org/quickstart/)** | A full-stack A2UI app with a backend and frontend. Learn A2UI end-to-end and customize to your use case. | ~5 min | | 🎨 **[A2UI Composer](https://a2ui-project.github.io/composer/)** | Generate A2UI JSON from a visual editor and paste it into any agent prompt — no install required. | ~1 min | | 🎬 **[A2UI Theater](https://a2ui-composer.ag-ui.com/theater)** | Step through pre-built A2UI streaming scenarios across Lit, React, and Angular renderers — no install required. | ~1 min | ## Packages These packages are developed in this repository. Packages marked "Not published yet" can be used from source. ### Python | Package | Description | Version | | ------------------------------------ | evaluation, and catalog validation. | [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/a2ui-core.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-core/) | | [a2ui-agent-sdk](python/a2ui_agent/) | Agent SDK: negotiates catalogs, generates prompts and skills, and compiles model output into A2UI. | [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/a2ui-agent-sdk.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-agent-sdk/) | | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@a2ui/catalog-mcp.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/catalog-mcp) | | [@a2ui/catalog-vegachart](typescript/catalogs/vegachart/) | VegaChart catalog: renders Vega and Vega-Lite chart specifications on A2UI surfaces. | Not published yet | ### Dart and Flutter | Package | Description | Version | | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [a2ui_core](dart/a2ui_core/) | Protocol messages, data model, data binding, and expressions for renderers and agents. | [![pub](https://img.shields.io/pub/v/a2ui_core.svg)](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_core) | | [a2ui_agent](dart/a2ui_agent/) | Agent SDK: negotiates catalogs, generates prompts and skills, and compiles model output into A2UI. | [![pub](https://img.shields.io/pub/v/a2ui_agent.svg)](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_agent) | | [a2ui_flutter](dart/a2ui_flutter/) | Flutter renderer. | [![pub](https://img.shields.io/pub/v/a2ui_flutter.svg)](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_flutter) | | [a2ui_cli](dart/a2ui_cli/) | Developer tool that generates typesafe component code from a catalog. | [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/releases) | ### Swift The Swift libraries are distributed via Swift Package Manager from [Package.swift](Package.swift) at the root of this repository. | Package | Description | | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | [A2UISwiftCore, BasicCatalog](swift/core/) | Message processor, data model, expression evaluation, and basic catalog definitions. | | [A2UISwiftUI, BasicCatalogSwiftUI](swift/swiftui/) | SwiftUI renderer and basic catalog views. | ## Roadmap - **Protocol v1.1**: We are collecting requirements for the next iteration of the A2UI protocol. - **Inference**: Support for decision models (e.g. Jev). - **Templates**: A cross-framework templating engine and a set of standard primitives for rendering reusable rich UI widgets. - **Sandboxed logic**: A way to securely attach logic to A2UI components. - **Agent SDK**: Skill generation, better diagnostics, and integrations with more agent frameworks. - **Evals**: A set of tools for evaluating generated UI quality. - **MCP Apps**: Embedding MCP Apps inside A2UI, and embedding A2UI experiences into MCP Apps. - **CLI**: Schema validation, codegen, local preview, and integration with coding agents. ## Contribute A2UI is an **Apache 2.0** licensed project. We believe the future of UI is agentic, and we want to work with you to help build it. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for details on how to get started.

repositories.name: trivy
repositories.description: Find vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, secrets, SBOM in containers, Kubernetes, code repositories, clouds and more
repositories.readme:
[![GitHub Release][release-img]][release] [![Test][test-img]][test] [![Go Report Card][go-report-img]][go-report] [![License: Apache-2.0][license-img]][license] [![GitHub Downloads][github-downloads-img]][release] ![Docker Pulls][docker-pulls] [📖 Documentation][docs]
Trivy ([pronunciation][pronunciation]) is a comprehensive and versatile security scanner. Trivy has *scanners* that look for security issues, and *targets* where it can find those issues. Targets (what Trivy can scan): - Container Image - Filesystem - Git Repository (remote) - Virtual Machine Image - Kubernetes Scanners (what Trivy can find there): - OS packages and software dependencies in use (SBOM) - Known vulnerabilities (CVEs) - IaC issues and misconfigurations - Sensitive information and secrets - Software licenses Trivy supports most popular programming languages, operating systems, and platforms. For a complete list, see the [Scanning Coverage] page. To learn more, go to the [Trivy homepage][homepage] for feature highlights, or to the [Documentation site][docs] for detailed information. ## Quick Start ### Get Trivy Trivy is available in most common distribution channels. The full list of installation options is available in the [Installation] page. Here are a few popular examples: - `brew install trivy` - `docker run aquasec/trivy` - Download binary from - See [Installation] for more Trivy is integrated with many popular platforms and applications. The complete list of integrations is available in the [Ecosystem] page. Here are a few popular examples: - [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy-action) - [Kubernetes operator](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy-operator) - [VS Code plugin](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy-vscode-extension) - See [Ecosystem] for more ### Canary builds There are canary builds ([Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/aquasec/trivy/tags?page=1&name=canary), [GitHub](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/pkgs/container/trivy/75776514?tag=canary), [ECR](https://gallery.ecr.aws/aquasecurity/trivy#canary) images and [binaries](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/actions/workflows/canary.yaml)) generated with every push to the main branch. Please be aware: canary builds might have critical bugs, so they are not recommended for use in production. ### General usage ```bash trivy [--scanners ] ``` Examples: ```bash trivy image python:3.4-alpine ```
Result https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af1c11e7-d9c5-48af-8e05-cb34dfd6352a
```bash trivy fs --scanners vuln,secret,misconfig myproject/ ```
Result https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b3894b7-77c5-4ffc-ac94-ffe6648a30dc
```bash trivy k8s --report summary cluster ```
Result ![k8s summary](docs/imgs/trivy-k8s.png)
## FAQ ### How to pronounce the name "Trivy"? `tri` is pronounced like **tri**gger, `vy` is pronounced like en**vy**. ## Want more? Check out Aqua If you liked Trivy, you will love Aqua which builds on top of Trivy to provide even more enhanced capabilities for a complete security management offering. You can find a high level comparison table specific to Trivy users [here](https://trivy.dev/docs/latest/commercial/compare/). In addition check out the website for more information about our products and services. If you'd like to contact Aqua or request a demo, please use this form: ## Community Trivy is an [Aqua Security][aquasec] open source project. Learn about our open source work and portfolio [here][oss]. Contact us about any matter by opening a GitHub Discussion [here][discussions] Please ensure to abide by our [Code of Conduct][code-of-conduct] during all interactions.
